title: EULAR recommendations for the management of rheumatoid arthritis with synthetic and biologic disease-modifying antirheumatic drugs: 2025 update.
key_finding: 2025 EULAR update: 5 principles, 9 recommendations; MTX + short-term GC first line; bDMARD after 3-6 mo insufficient response; JAKi after risk assessment; tapering possible but stopping often causes flare

title: EULAR recommendations for the management of rheumatoid arthritis with synthetic and biological disease-modifying antirheumatic drugs: 2022 update.
key_finding: 2022 EULAR update: 5 principles, 11 recommendations; stratification by poor prognostic factors; 'DMARDs may be tapered but should not be stopped'

title: 2021 American College of Rheumatology Guideline for the Treatment of Rheumatoid Arthritis.
key_finding: 2021 ACR guideline: 44 recommendations, 7 strong and 37 conditional - most of the treatment algorithm rests on low-certainty evidence

title: Treating rheumatoid arthritis to target: 2014 update of the recommendations of an international task force.
key_finding: Treat-to-target 2014 update: 4 principles, 10 recommendations; target remission, LDA acceptable alternative in long-standing disease; review every 1-3 months while active

title: 2010 Rheumatoid arthritis classification criteria: an American College of Rheumatology/European League Against Rheumatism collaborative initiative.
key_finding: 2010 ACR/EULAR classification criteria: score >=6/10 across joint involvement, serology, acute-phase reactants, symptom duration

title: American College of Rheumatology/European League Against Rheumatism provisional definition of remission in rheumatoid arthritis for clinical trials.
key_finding: 2011 ACR/EULAR provisional remission definition (Boolean and index-based)

title: American College of Rheumatology/EULAR remission criteria for rheumatoid arthritis: 2022 revision.
key_finding: 2022 revision: Boolean2.0 (PtGA <=2 cm) raised 6-month remission from 14.8% to 20.6% (early RA) and 4.2% to 6.0% (established RA) without loss of predictive value

title: Global, regional, and national burden of rheumatoid arthritis, 1990-2020, and projections to 2050: a systematic analysis of the Global Burden of Disease Study 2021.
key_finding: GBD 2021: 17.6M (15.8-20.3) cases in 2020; age-standardised prevalence 208.8/100k (+14.1% since 1990); F:M 2.45; 38,300 deaths (death rate -23.8% since 1990); projected 31.7M by 2050

title: Global, regional and national burden of rheumatoid arthritis 1990-2017: a systematic analysis of the Global Burden of Disease study 2017.
key_finding: GBD 2017: age-standardised prevalence 246.6/100k, incidence 14.9/100k; DALY rate 43.3 (-3.6% since 1990) - note discrepancy with GBD 2021 estimates

title: Rheumatoid arthritis.
key_finding: Lancet Seminar 2023: current state of RA diagnosis, pathogenesis and management

title: The pathogenesis of rheumatoid arthritis.
key_finding: RA is the end of a multi-year prodrome; unmet needs include non-response, failure to achieve drug-free remission, inability to repair tissue

title: Genetics of rheumatoid arthritis contributes to biology and drug discovery.
key_finding: 29,880 cases / 73,758 controls; 42 novel loci (101 total); 98 candidate genes; RA loci enriched for approved drug targets

title: On the origin of rheumatoid arthritis: the impact of environment and genes--a population based twin study.
key_finding: Population twin study: MZ concordance 9.1% (1.9-24.3), DZ 6.4%; additive genetic 12% (0-76%), shared environment 50% (0-72%), non-shared 38% (17-61%) - much wider uncertainty than the often-quoted ~60% heritability

title: Gene-environment interaction between the DRB1 shared epitope and smoking in the risk of anti-citrullinated protein antibody-positive rheumatoid arthritis: all alleles are important.
key_finding: HLA-DRB1 shared epitope x smoking interaction for ACPA-positive RA: RR 8.7 (5.7-13.1) for DRB1*04 alleles; attributable proportion due to interaction 0.4-0.6

title: Systematic Review and Meta-analysis on the Association of Occupational Exposure to Free Crystalline Silica and Rheumatoid Arthritis.
key_finding: Occupational crystalline silica: RA OR 1.94 (1.46-2.58); association in both seropositive and seronegative disease

title: Exposure to Occupational Inhalants and the Risk of Developing Rheumatoid Arthritis: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
key_finding: Occupational inhalants (31 studies): silica, asbestos, solvents, pesticides, fertilizers, animal dust, engine exhaust all associated with RA, RR 1.25-1.49

title: Antibodies against cyclic citrullinated peptide and IgA rheumatoid factor predict the development of rheumatoid arthritis.
key_finding: Anti-CCP and RF detectable in stored blood a median 2.5 years before symptom onset; anti-CCP sensitivity 25% >1.5 y and 52% <=1.5 y before symptoms

title: Distinct mucosal endotypes as initiators and drivers of rheumatoid arthritis.
key_finding: ACPA seropositivity precedes clinical RA by an average of 3-5 years; multiple distinct mucosal endotypes proposed as initiators

title: Rheumatoid arthritis and the mucosal origins hypothesis: protection turns to destruction.
key_finding: Mucosal origins hypothesis; more at-risk individuals show mucosal ACPA production than ever develop RA, raising the possibility of a protective role

title: The gut-joint axis in rheumatoid arthritis.
key_finding: Gut-joint axis: dysbiosis reported in preclinical and established RA; causal direction unresolved

title: The oral and gut microbiomes are perturbed in rheumatoid arthritis and partly normalized after treatment.
key_finding: Oral and gut dysbiosis in RA, partially normalised after treatment; Haemophilus depleted, Lactobacillus salivarius enriched

title: EULAR/American College of Rheumatology Risk Stratification Criteria for Development of Rheumatoid Arthritis in the Risk Stage of Arthralgia.
key_finding: EULAR/ACR risk stratification criteria in arthralgia (n=2,293): 6 clinical/serologic variables AUC 0.80; adding MRI 0.87 for inflammatory arthritis and 0.93 for RA

title: Benefit of very early referral and very early therapy with disease-modifying anti-rheumatic drugs in patients with early rheumatoid arthritis.
key_finding: Very early (median 3 mo) versus late early (12 mo) DMARD start: DAS28 improvement 2.8 vs 1.7 at 36 months, less radiographic progression

title: Absent "Window of Opportunity" in smokers with short disease duration. Data from BARFOT, a multicenter study of early rheumatoid arthritis.
key_finding: BARFOT (n=1,587): shorter symptom duration predicted better EULAR response - but no such gradient in smokers

title: Effect of a treatment strategy of tight control for rheumatoid arthritis (the TICORA study): a single-blind randomised controlled trial.
key_finding: TICORA: intensive tight control vs routine care - good response 82% vs 44%, DAS28 remission 65% vs 16%

title: Comparison of treatment strategies in early rheumatoid arthritis: a randomized trial.
key_finding: BeSt 2-year: all four strategies converged; 42% in remission; initial combination therapy better suppressed joint damage

title: Active conventional treatment and three different biological treatments in early rheumatoid arthritis: phase IV investigator initiated, randomised, observer blinded clinical trial.
key_finding: NORD-STAR 24-week primary outcome comparing active conventional therapy with three biologics in treatment-naive early RA

title: Certolizumab pegol, abatacept, tocilizumab or active conventional treatment in early rheumatoid arthritis: 48-week clinical and radiographic results of the investigator-initiated randomised controlled NORD-STAR trial.
key_finding: NORD-STAR 48-week CDAI remission: abatacept 59.3%, certolizumab 52.3%, tocilizumab 51.9%, active conventional therapy 39.2%

title: Low rates of remission with methotrexate monotherapy in rheumatoid arthritis: review of randomised controlled trials could point towards a paradigm shift.
key_finding: Methotrexate monotherapy yields remission in at most about half of patients across RCTs

journal: The Cochrane database of systematic reviews
title: Disease-modifying antirheumatic drugs (DMARDs) for rheumatoid arthritis after failure of biologic or targeted synthetic therapy: a systematic review and network meta-analysis.
key_finding: 19 RCTs, 4,779 participants after b/tsDMARD failure; ACR50 vs placebo: a not-previously-tried TNF inhibitor OR 6.04 (2.49-16.3, high certainty); IL-6 inhibitors, abatacept, rituximab, JAK inhibitors also effective

title: Risk of serious infection in biological treatment of patients with rheumatoid arthritis: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
key_finding: Serious infection vs traditional DMARDs: standard-dose biologics OR 1.31 (1.09-1.58); high-dose 1.90 (1.50-2.39); low-dose 0.93 (0.65-1.33)

journal: The New England journal of medicine
title: Cardiovascular and Cancer Risk with Tofacitinib in Rheumatoid Arthritis.
key_finding: ORAL Surveillance: tofacitinib vs TNF inhibitor in CV-risk-enriched RA - MACE HR 1.33 (0.91-1.94), cancer HR 1.48 (1.04-2.09); non-inferiority not shown

title: Low dose, add-on prednisolone in patients with rheumatoid arthritis aged 65+: the pragmatic randomised, double-blind placebo-controlled GLORIA trial.
key_finding: GLORIA: prednisolone 5 mg/day for 2 years in patients 65+ lowered DAS28 by 0.37 and damage progression by 1.7 points, with 24% relative increase in patients having an adverse event of interest (mostly non-severe infections)

title: Global inequities in biologic and targeted DMARD use in rheumatoid arthritis: cross-sectional data from the international COVAD-2 cohort.
key_finding: COVAD-2 (n=1,997 RA): advanced therapy use 29.6% overall - Europe 44.0%, Asia 11.7%, Africa 5.3%; 2.7% in low-HDI vs 38.8% in very-high-HDI countries

title: EULAR definition of difficult-to-treat rheumatoid arthritis.
key_finding: EULAR D2T RA definition: failure of >=2 b/tsDMARDs with different mechanisms, plus active/progressive disease or QoL impact, plus perceived problematic management

title: EULAR points to consider for the management of difficult-to-treat rheumatoid arthritis.
key_finding: EULAR points to consider for D2T RA: 2 principles, 11 points; strength of recommendation only C-D throughout

title: Difficult-to-treat rheumatoid arthritis: systematic review and meta-analysis on global prevalence.
key_finding: 23 studies, 27,987 patients: pooled D2T prevalence 11.7% (9.5-14.3); ~47.1% of D2T show persistent inflammatory refractory disease; >=3 b/tsDMARD failures 4.3%; >=4 failures 1.6%

title: Poly-Refractory Rheumatoid Arthritis: An Uncommon Subset of Difficult to Treat Disease With Distinct Inflammatory and Noninflammatory Phenotypes.
key_finding: n=1,469: D2T 16.8%, poly-refractory (all classes failed) 2.7%; among D2T with ultrasound, 57% PIRRA and 43% NIRRA; NIRRA had higher BMI and fibromyalgia prevalence

title: Persistent inflammatory and non-inflammatory mechanisms in refractory rheumatoid arthritis.
key_finding: Conceptual separation of persistent inflammatory refractory RA (PIRRA) from non-inflammatory refractory RA (NIRRA), with different management implications

title: Difficult-to-treat rheumatoid arthritis: contributing factors and burden of disease.
key_finding: D2T patients (n=52 vs 100 controls): lower socioeconomic status at onset OR 1.97; limited drug options from adverse events 94% vs 57%, comorbidity 69% vs 37%, concomitant fibromyalgia 38% vs 9%

title: Biologic refractory disease in rheumatoid arthritis: results from the British Society for Rheumatology Biologics Register for Rheumatoid Arthritis.
key_finding: BSRBR-RA (n=13,502): 6% reached a third bDMARD class ('biologic refractory'), median 8 years; associated with female sex, smoking, obesity, deprivation

title: Rituximab versus tocilizumab in anti-TNF inadequate responder patients with rheumatoid arthritis (R4RA): 16-week outcomes of a stratified, biopsy-driven, multicentre, open-label, phase 4 randomised controlled trial.
key_finding: R4RA: in histologically B-cell-poor synovium no significant difference (CDAI50 45% rituximab vs 56% tocilizumab); in RNA-seq-defined B-cell-poor synovium tocilizumab superior (63% vs 36%, difference 26% [2-50])

title: Rituximab versus tocilizumab in rheumatoid arthritis: synovial biopsy-based biomarker analysis of the phase 4 R4RA randomized trial.
key_finding: R4RA molecular analysis: ~40% do not respond to an individual biologic and 5-20% are refractory to all; stromal/fibroblast signature marks multidrug resistance; ML AUC 0.74 (rituximab), 0.68 (tocilizumab), 0.69 (multidrug resistance)

title: Deep molecular profiling of synovial biopsies in the STRAP trial identifies signatures predictive of treatment response to biologic therapies in rheumatoid arthritis.
key_finding: STRAP (n=208): synovial RNA-seq models predicted response AUC 0.75-0.76; external validation in R4RA AUC 0.71-0.79; 524-gene panel AUC 0.82-0.87 - not yet prospectively tested as a treatment-allocation tool

title: Deconstruction of rheumatoid arthritis synovium defines inflammatory subtypes.
key_finding: 79 donors, >314,000 cells; six cell-type abundance phenotypes (CTAPs) spanning lymphocyte-rich to lymphocyte-poor synovium; CTAPs are dynamic and associate with treatment response

title: Spatial patterning of fibroblast TGFβ signaling underlies treatment resistance in rheumatoid arthritis.
key_finding: Non-remitting patients showed fibrogenic vascular niches with high fibroblast COMP and endothelial Notch-driven TGFbeta signalling; post-treatment immune depletion with expansion of fibrogenic niches - hypothesis-generating target

title: Distinct synovial tissue macrophage subsets regulate inflammation and remission in rheumatoid arthritis.
key_finding: MerTK+TREM2+ and MerTK+LYVE1+ synovial macrophage subsets carry remission signatures; a low MerTK+ proportion in remission was associated with increased flare risk after treatment cessation

title: Single-cell insights into immune dysregulation in rheumatoid arthritis flare versus drug-free remission.
key_finding: Drug withdrawal used to synchronise flare: three circulating subsets herald flare onset; Treg numbers rise but with dysfunctional marker expression; clonal T-cell (not B-cell) expansion after drug cessation

title: Persistence of Disease-Associated Anti-Citrullinated Protein Antibody-Expressing Memory B Cells in Rheumatoid Arthritis in Clinical Remission.
key_finding: ACPA-expressing switched-memory B cells persist in patients in clinical remission

title: Autoreactive B cells remain active despite clinical disease control in rheumatoid arthritis.
key_finding: ACPA+ memory B cells retain a highly activated phenotype despite effective clinical disease control, including under JAK inhibition

title: Subclinical Synovitis Assessed by Ultrasound Predicts Flare and Progressive Bone Erosion in Rheumatoid Arthritis Patients with Clinical Remission: A Systematic Review and Metaanalysis.
key_finding: Power Doppler positivity in clinical remission: flare OR 4.52 (2.61-7.84); progressive erosion OR 12.80 (patient level) and 11.85 (joint level)

title: Effect of Half-Dose vs Stable-Dose Conventional Synthetic Disease-Modifying Antirheumatic Drugs on Disease Flares in Patients With Rheumatoid Arthritis in Remission: The ARCTIC REWIND Randomized Clinical Trial.
key_finding: ARCTIC REWIND: half-dose vs stable csDMARDs in >=12 months' remission, 12-month flare comparison (non-inferiority margin 20%)

title: Effects of tapering conventional synthetic disease-modifying antirheumatic drugs to drug-free remission versus stable treatment in rheumatoid arthritis (ARCTIC REWIND): 3-year results from an open-label, randomised controlled, non-inferiority trial.
key_finding: ARCTIC REWIND 3-year: stable vs half-dose vs half-dose-then-withdrawal csDMARDs

title: Effect of tapered versus stable treatment with tumour necrosis factor inhibitors on disease flares in patients with rheumatoid arthritis in remission: a randomised, open label, non-inferiority trial.
key_finding: ARCTIC REWIND TNFi: tapering to withdrawal caused flare in 27/43 (63%) vs 2/41 (5%) on stable therapy; risk difference 58% (42-74) - tapering was NOT non-inferior

title: Sustained DMARD-free remission in subgroups of patients with rheumatoid arthritis: an analysis of two prospective cohorts with early arthritis.
key_finding: Leiden EAC and tREACH: no patient who ever needed a bDMARD achieved sustained DMARD-free remission, versus 37% (5 y, EAC) and 15% (3 y, tREACH) of those who never did - suggests the blanket 'do not stop' recommendation may reflect ascertainment bias

title: The likelihood of attaining and maintaining DMARD-free remission for various (rheumatoid) arthritis phenotypes.
key_finding: tREACH: DMARD-free remission at 2-5 y was 17.2-25.7% in autoantibody-positive RA, 28.4-42.1% in autoantibody-negative RA and 43.1-58.5% in undifferentiated arthritis; sustained DFR 7.6-21.4%, 20.5-38.1% and 35.4-55.4% respectively

title: Long-Term Outcomes in Seronegative Rheumatoid Arthritis.
key_finding: Olmsted County (n=176 seronegative RA): 10-year cumulative incidence of diagnosis change 12.8%, drug-free remission 26.6%, b/tsDMARD start 19.9%

title: Effects of B-cell directed therapy on the preclinical stage of rheumatoid arthritis: the PRAIRI study.
key_finding: PRAIRI: single 1000 mg rituximab infusion in ACPA+/RF+ individuals delayed arthritis onset by 12 months; HR 0.45 (0.154-1.322) at 12 months - delay, not prevention

title: Intervention with methotrexate in patients with arthralgia at risk of rheumatoid arthritis to reduce the development of persistent arthritis and its disease burden (TREAT EARLIER): a randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled, proof-of-concept trial.
key_finding: TREAT EARLIER: 1 year of methotrexate + single GC injection in clinically suspect arthralgia with subclinical inflammation did NOT prevent arthritis at 2 years (19% vs 18%, HR 0.81 [0.45-1.48]) but sustainedly improved HAQ, pain, stiffness, presenteeism and MRI inflammation

title: Long-term durability of a time-limited methotrexate intervention in patients with anti-citrullinated protein antibody-positive and anti-citrullinated protein antibody-negative arthralgia at increased risk for rheumatoid arthritis (TREAT EARLIER): 5-year data from a double-blind, randomised, placebo-controlled trial.
key_finding: TREAT EARLIER 5-year: in ACPA-NEGATIVE at-risk participants, RA developed in 3/35 (9%) vs 10/31 (32%), HR 0.24 (0.07-0.87), NNT 4; in ACPA-positive participants no effect (58% vs 65%, HR 0.75 [0.38-1.49])

title: Abatacept in individuals at high risk of rheumatoid arthritis (APIPPRA): a randomised, double-blind, multicentre, parallel, placebo-controlled, phase 2b clinical trial.
key_finding: APIPPRA: 12 months of abatacept in ACPA+/RF+ arthralgia - primary endpoint met in 6% vs 29% during treatment; 25% vs 37% progressed to RA by 24 months; benefit not sustained after treatment stopped

title: Long-term outcomes of abatacept in individuals at risk of developing rheumatoid arthritis (ALTO): a randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial.
key_finding: ALTO (APIPPRA extension, median 55 months): the arthritis-free survival difference persisted at 4 years (4.9 months, 95% CI 0.1-9.6) but diminished; participants with a broad autoantibody profile were both highest risk and most responsive

journal: The New England journal of medicine
title: Olokizumab versus Placebo or Adalimumab in Rheumatoid Arthritis.
key_finding: Olokizumab (direct IL-6 targeting) phase 3: ACR20 at week 12 70.3% (q2w) vs 44.4% placebo, tested for non-inferiority to adalimumab

title: Anti-GM-CSF otilimab versus tofacitinib or placebo in patients with active rheumatoid arthritis and an inadequate response to conventional or biologic DMARDs: two phase 3 randomised trials (contRAst 1 and contRAst 2).
key_finding: Otilimab (anti-GM-CSF) contRAst 1/2: ACR20 54.7%/50.9% vs 41.7% placebo and 54.9%/54.5% vs 32.5% placebo - statistically significant but modest

journal: The New England journal of medicine
title: A Phase 2 Trial of Peresolimab for Adults with Rheumatoid Arthritis.
key_finding: Peresolimab, a PD-1 agonist antibody - first clinical test of deliberately stimulating an inhibitory immune checkpoint in RA

title: Vagus nerve-mediated neuroimmune modulation for rheumatoid arthritis: a pivotal randomized controlled trial.
key_finding: RESET-RA (n=242, inadequate response to b/tsDMARDs): vagus nerve stimulation ACR20 35.2% vs 24.2% sham at 3 months (p=0.0209); 52.8% at 12 months open-label; related serious adverse events 1.6%, all perioperative

title: CAR T-cell therapy in autoimmune diseases.
key_finding: CAR T-cell therapy in autoimmune disease - RA experience minimal to date

title: Systematic Literature Review of Residual Symptoms and an Unmet Need in Patients With Rheumatoid Arthritis.
key_finding: 55 records: residual functional disability, tender/swollen joints, pain, fatigue and impaired patient global persist in a substantial fraction of patients meeting remission or LDA targets

title: Residual pain in rheumatoid arthritis: Is it a real problem?
key_finding: Residual pain persists after inflammation is controlled; central sensitisation and comorbid fibromyalgia contribute

title: Prevalence of comorbidities in rheumatoid arthritis and evaluation of their monitoring: results of an international, cross-sectional study (COMORA).
key_finding: COMORA (3,920 patients, 17 countries): depression 15%, asthma 6.6%, myocardial infarction/stroke 6%, solid malignancy 4.5%, COPD 3.5%; wide between-country variation in preventive care

title: Risk of cardiovascular mortality in patients with rheumatoid arthritis: a meta-analysis of observational studies.
key_finding: Cardiovascular mortality meta-SMR 1.50 (1.39-1.61); ischaemic heart disease 1.59; cerebrovascular 1.52; inception cohorts alone not significant (1.19, 0.86-1.68)

title: The widening mortality gap between rheumatoid arthritis patients and the general population.
key_finding: Rochester/Olmsted 1955-2000: RA mortality rates did not fall in parallel with the general population, widening the mortality gap

title: Improvement in 5-year mortality in incident rheumatoid arthritis compared with the general population-closing the mortality gap.
key_finding: British Columbia incident cohorts 1996-2000 vs 2001-2006: 5-year mortality relative to matched controls improved in the later cohort - reported as closing the mortality gap

title: A population-based cohort study of rheumatoid arthritis-associated interstitial lung disease: comorbidity and mortality.
key_finding: Denmark: RA-ILD in 2.2% of incident RA; 1-year mortality 13.9% vs 3.8%, 5-year 39.0% vs 18.2%, 10-year 60.1% vs 34.5%; hazard ratios 2-10x

title: Updated systematic literature review and meta-analysis to inform the Italian Society of Rheumatology Recommendations on the treatment of rheumatoid arthritis-associated interstitial lung disease.
key_finding: 69 studies, 7,879 RA-ILD patients: methotrexate associated with reduced ILD progression and mortality; abatacept, rituximab and nintedanib identified as promising; evidence largely observational

title: Prevention and cure: The major unmet needs in the management of rheumatoid arthritis.
key_finding: Prevention and cure framed as the two major unmet needs in RA management

title: Diagnostic, prognostic and therapeutic biomarkers in rheumatoid arthritis.
key_finding: Sustained remission is achieved by only a minority; delays in diagnosis, imprecise risk stratification and suboptimal treatment selection identified as causes; no biomarker is yet in routine use for treatment selection
